notes.Naji Marshall: Cooper Flagg is out with a shoulder injury, and Marshall had 15 points, six assists and three steals in 33 minutes off the bench on Friday.
notes.PJ Washington: He had 20 points, 13 rebounds and three blocks in 33 minutes on Friday, and Cooper Flagg is out tonight.
notes.Zaccharie Risacher: He played 32 minutes on Friday after Cooper Flagg went down, with three blocks, and Flagg is out tonight.
notes.Kyrie Irving: He scored 24 points in 25 minutes on Friday, and tonight is the second night of a back-to-back, so check that he plays.
notes.Joel Embiid: Philadelphia plays tonight and again Sunday, and Embiid is likely to sit one of the two games, so check his status before lock.
notes.Derik Queen: Yves Missi hurt his knee on Friday, and Queen played 29 minutes with 12 points, seven rebounds, two steals and two blocks.
notes.Fred VanVleet: He played 32 minutes on Friday, and tonight is the second night of a back-to-back, so he is a sit risk.
notes.Marcus Smart: If Fred VanVleet sits the second night of the back-to-back, Smart starts at guard.
notes.Brandin Podziemski: He came back on Friday and started, playing 33 minutes.
notes.Yaxel Lendeborg: He played 37 minutes on Friday with 18 points, 13 rebounds and six assists, and Golden State is on the second night of a back-to-back.
notes.Stephen Curry: He played 30 minutes on Friday, and tonight is the second night of a back-to-back.
notes.Khaman Maluach: Oso Ighodaro is doubtful with an oblique injury, which leaves more of the center minutes for Maluach.
notes.Keon Ellis: Brooklyn plays tonight and Sunday, and Mikel Brown Jr. is on a minutes limit.
He is on a minutes limit and is expected to play tonight and sit Sunday.
notes.Leonard Miller: He played 24 minutes as the backup center on Friday and scored 19 points, but his 7-of-11 shooting will be hard to repeat.
notes.Jalen Smith: He had 14 points, 13 rebounds and three steals in 24 minutes on Friday while Nic Claxton is out.
notes.Victor Wembanyama: He had 25 points and 13 rebounds in 32 minutes in Friday's four-point loss to Houston, and Tobias Harris (calf) is out again. Tonight is the second night of a back-to-back, and Dallas has no Cooper Flagg or Dereck Lively II up front.
notes.Donovan Mitchell: He had 32 points and 10 rebounds in 35 minutes in the opener on Thursday, and Cleveland is rested while Brooklyn comes in for its first game since Wednesday. The 11.5-point spread is the one worry for his minutes.
notes.Tyrese Maxey: He has played 40 and 42 minutes in Philadelphia's first two games, with 32 points on Thursday. Philadelphia plays again Sunday and Joel Embiid is likely to sit one of the two games, which would put even more of the offense in Maxey's hands.
notes.Alperen Sengun: He scored 29 points in 36 minutes Friday, including eight straight in the fourth quarter, by muscling inside for layups and free throws. Reed Sheppard is out, and Houston is on the second night of a back-to-back.
notes.Jalen Johnson: He had 19 points, eight assists, seven rebounds and three steals in only 29 minutes Friday because the 47-point blowout ended early. Tonight should be a real game against Houston, so his minutes should climb back up.
notes.Jaylon Tyson: He played 24 minutes off the bench in the opener and filled the box with six rebounds and two blocks. Cleveland is short on depth with Khalifa Diop and Nae'Qwan Tomlin out, and a big lead would mean more bench minutes.
notes.Sam Merrill: He played 24 minutes off the bench in the opener, and Cleveland's thin bench keeps him in the rotation every night. A blowout of Brooklyn would mean more late minutes for him.
notes.Kyle Kuzma: He has started both games and had 14 points, nine rebounds and four assists in 30 minutes Friday. Milwaukee is on the second night of a back-to-back, so check the starting five.
notes.Kingston Flemings: The rookie backup point guard jumped from 15 minutes in the opener to 25 on Friday, with eight assists and six rebounds. Some of that came in a blowout, so 20 or so minutes is the safer guess tonight.
He played 17 minutes off the bench Friday with eight points and six rebounds. Cooper Flagg and Dereck Lively II are out and Daniel Gafford played only 15 minutes Friday, so the Dallas frontcourt minutes are wide open.
notes.Max Christie: He has started both games and played 38 minutes Friday with 16 points after Cooper Flagg went out. Flagg is out tonight, so Christie should stay near the top of the Dallas minutes list.
notes.Keldon Johnson: He played 19 minutes off the bench Friday with eight points and six rebounds, and Tobias Harris is still out. San Antonio is on a back-to-back, which could spread the minutes a little more.
notes.Luke Kornet: He is the backup center and played 16 minutes Friday with seven points. Tobias Harris is out, and the second night of a back-to-back could mean a few more minutes behind Victor Wembanyama.
notes.Al Horford: He played 19 minutes Friday, and he is not expected to play back-to-backs, so he could sit tonight in Phoenix.
notes.Dyson Daniels: He had seven steals and nine rebounds in only 23 minutes during Friday's blowout of Charlotte.
